## Presentations

Both sessions this week are team presentations, with partner-organization representatives
invited to attend.

**Format.** 12 minutes presenting, 5 minutes questions, 3 minutes changeover. Timing is
enforced — a project manager who cannot brief a sponsor inside a fixed slot has a problem
that is not about slides.

**Required content**, in any order that serves your argument:

- The project, the partner, and what success meant *to them* — on which dimensions.
- Your delivery approach and the alternative you rejected, with the reason.
- The quantitative spine: WBS, schedule model, budget baseline, and where actuals diverged.
- The risk that materialized, or the one you were most wrong about.
- **The AI section:** what your agent maintained, what it got wrong, how you caught it, and
  the control you would put in place to govern it over two years.

The AI section is not an appendix. Teams that treat it as one lose the marks attached to the
sixth course objective.

::: {.callout-important}
## Partner attendance
Confirm with your partner contact by **Friday 27 November** whether they will attend in person,
join remotely, or receive the recording. Nothing about your grade depends on their attendance —
but the invitation is part of the professional obligation of the engagement.
:::

## Course close — Thursday

The last twenty minutes are a debrief on the course itself: what the evidence base actually
supports, what remains genuinely contested, and which of the tools you learned you should
expect to still be using in ten years. Bring disagreements.

## Final report

Due **Friday 11 December, 11:59 p.m.** See [Final Project](../project.qmd) for the required
structure and the rubric.
